record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
record.original_question: Given a real symmetric matrix X that is not in CP_n, construct a copositive matrix Y in COP_n such that trace(XY) < 0. Here CP_n is the cone of real symmetric n x n matrices A = B B^T with B entrywise nonnegative, and COP_n is the cone of real symmetric n x n matrices Y satisfying z^T Y z >= 0 for every z in R_+^n; such a Y gives a cutting plane separating X from CP_n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{S}^n$ denote the space of real symmetric $n\times n$ matrices, and let $\mathbb{R}_+^n$ denote the nonnegative orthant of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Define the cone of completely positive matrices
$$\mathrm{CP}_n := \{A\in\mathcal{S}^n : A = BB^T \text{ for some entrywise nonnegative matrix } B\},$$
and the cone of copositive matrices
$$\mathrm{COP}_n := \{Y\in\mathcal{S}^n : z^T Y z \ge 0 \text{ for all } z\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\}.$$
These cones are dual with respect to the trace inner product $\langle X, Y\rangle = \mathrm{tr}(XY)$.

Problem. Devise a constructive procedure with the following property: given any symmetric matrix $X\in\mathcal{S}^n$ that does not lie in $\mathrm{CP}_n$, the procedure produces a copositive matrix $Y\in\mathrm{COP}_n$ such that
$$\mathrm{tr}(XY) < 0.$$
Such a $Y$ furnishes a separating hyperplane (a cutting plane) between $X$ and the completely positive cone $\mathrm{CP}_n$.
artifact.status_search_result: Several partial results address this separation question. Berman and Dür gave explicit constructions of separating copositive cuts for $5\times 5$ doubly nonnegative but non-completely-positive matrices. Bundfuss–Dür and Sponsel–Dür developed factorization and cutting-plane methods using polyhedral inner/outer approximations of the cones, and an analytic center cutting plane method (Badenbroek–de Klerk, 2020) detects non-membership and returns a separating cut, with the membership oracle reducing to a mixed-integer linear program. A general efficient/explicit construction valid for arbitrary $n$ remains elusive, so the problem is best regarded as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Separating doubly nonnegative and completely positive matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Two different constructions of separating cuts described for 5x5 doubly nonnegative but non-completely-positive matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Partial constructive separation results exist for small dimensions.

status_evidence.title: An Analytic Center Cutting Plane Method to Determine Complete Positivity of a Matrix
status_evidence.snippet: Analytic center cutting plane method optimizing over intersection of a ball with the copositive cone, returning a cut separating a non-CP matrix from CP_n.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithmic separating procedures have been developed.

status_evidence.title: Factorization and cutting planes for completely positive matrices by copositive projection
status_evidence.snippet: Cutting plane techniques using polyhedral approximations of the cones to compute CP factorizations.
status_evidence.claim: Cutting-plane / projection methods give partial constructive answers.
